sights.address: Blk 570 Ang Mo Kio Avenue 3, Singapore 560570
sights.w: One of the last surviving vintage sand-pit dragon playgrounds in Singapore — a 1980s reproduction of the beloved Toa Payoh design, its dragon head clad in terrazzo mosaic tiles, spine of steel rails, and (uniquely to this one) a mosaic slide. A stop on the Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail's Iconic Landmarks route and a nostalgic icon of heartland childhood.

sights.address: Ang Mo Kio Avenue 1 vicinity, Singapore (Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail; exact street to confirm)
sights.w: Established in 1978 and rebuilt in 2011, this joint temple houses three deities' temples displaced when their villages were cleared in the 1970s — Gao Lin Gong, Kim Eang Tong and Leng San Giam. The oldest, Gao Lin Gong, was founded in 1888 by Huang-surname immigrants from Nan An, Fujian, at Kow Tiow Kio ('nine bridges') along today's Ang Mo Kio Avenue 1; its pillars and facade carry carvings handcrafted by artisans in China. An Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail hidden gem.

sights.address: Ang Mo Kio / Yio Chu Kang vicinity (near Lentor Avenue), Singapore (Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail)
sights.w: Completed in 1989, this joint temple unites three temples — Sam Ann Fu, Longxuyan Jinshuiguan and the Hong San Chin Huat Temple Association — that once stood at Lak Xun, a village in Yio Chu Kang near present-day Lentor Avenue. One of two new markers added to the refreshed Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail in 2023, recording the town's transformation from plantation land to new town.

sights.address: Ang Mo Kio (Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail hidden gem; exact street to confirm)
sights.w: A clan temple and association for people of the Hong (Xiong) surname, first established in 1905 at Buona Vista and relocated over the decades to Ang Mo Kio — a rare surviving surname-clan temple and a Hidden Heartland Gems stop on the Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail, illustrating the village-and-clan networks that predate the new town.
